note: Each parsed ini option line is duplicated into heap memory before option parsing.
The duplicated option strings are copied again and prepared for keyword substitution.
The current option string is duplicated so substitutions can be applied on a writable heap buffer.
The parser searches the option string for reserved keywords such as $ncpus to replace them with runtime values.
The original heap pointer is saved so it can be freed after substitution.
When the keyword is not at the start of the string, opt is advanced past the keyword and prefix, so it no longer points to the allocation base.

code: if (strlen(opt)) memcpy(new + olen + len, opt, opt - o_org - 1);
note: The code computes the tail length from the advanced pointer and copies from opt, which can read past the intended source region and overflow the destination heap buffer.
